transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... I’m having trouble staying with things at work. Like I’ll start an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting, and I mean to pay attention, but a few minutes later I realize I’ve drifted off. Then I’m rereading the same numbers or I’ve missed the point of what people were saying. That’s what finally made me come in.
Have you always had trouble like this with focus and attention, even back in school or early in your career, or is this something that's started more recently?

No, it’s not brand new. I mean… I did well enough in school, so I didn’t really think of it that way. But even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I was “bright but careless.” My mom had to sit with me while I finished homework because I’d lose track of assignments or leave books at school. So… yes, I guess it goes back pretty far.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?
Not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad or stopped enjoying things.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—more than most people would—and having trouble controlling that worry?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about work things when I’m behind, but not… all kinds of things all the time. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you feel excessively sleepy or have trouble staying awake during the day, even after what should be a full night's sleep?
Not really. I mean, I get tired sometimes like anyone, but I don’t usually feel like I’m going to fall asleep during the day if I slept enough.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, longstanding inattentive symptoms (losing focus during meetings/reports, rereading material, missing key points) dating back to elementary school ('bright but careless,' needing supervision to complete homework, losing assignments).
